sect3.title: Using "namespace" as a class constant name
sect3.simpara: Declaring a class constant named namespace is now deprecated. namespace is a semi-reserved keyword, and the name is being reserved for possible future syntax such as a ::namespace pseudo-constant analogous to ::class. Methods and static properties named namespace are not affected. Rename the constant, for example to NAMESPACE_NAME.

sect3.title: Returning from a finally block
sect3.simpara: Using the return statement inside a finally block is now deprecated, and emits a compile-time deprecation notice. Such a return silently discards an exception thrown by, or overwrites the value returned from, the associated try or catch block, so failures vanish without a trace. Move the return out of the finally block instead; the same result can always be expressed without it.

informalexample.programlisting:
<?php
function getConfig(): array
{
    try {
        return loadConfig(); // throws if the file is missing
    } finally {
        return []; // Deprecated: the exception is gone, the caller just gets []
    }
}

sect3.title: Nullable return type for __debugInfo()
sect3.simpara: Declaring a return type of arraynull for __debugInfo() is now deprecated. Returning &null; from this method was already deprecated in PHP 8.5, so the nullable return type no longer describes valid behaviour. Declare array instead.

sect3.title: Returning values from __construct() and __destruct()
sect3.simpara: Returning a value from __construct() or __destruct() is now deprecated, and emits a compile-time deprecation notice. These methods cannot declare a return type, and their return value can never be observed during normal use, which made returning a value confusing at best. Using return; without a value to skip the remaining logic is still allowed, as is calling these methods manually.
For the same reason, using yield to make __construct() or __destruct() a generator is now deprecated.

sect3.title: Naming a function readonly
sect3.simpara: Declaring a function named readonly is now deprecated. readonly is a reserved keyword; a lexer exception was added in PHP 8.1 solely to keep an existing WordPress function of that name working, and no other keyword in PHP receives such special treatment. Rename the function.

sect3.title: Using let, is, or _ as an identifier
sect3.simpara: Using let or is as the name of a class, interface, trait, enum, function, or constant (including via define) is now deprecated, as is using either as the alias in a class_alias call or in a use, use function, or use const declaration. The names are being reserved as keywords for potential future features: let for block scoping and is for pattern matching. Rename the affected symbols.

The deprecation of _ as a class name in PHP 8.4 is extended to constants: declaring a constant named _ with const or define, and aliasing a class or constant to _ in a use declaration, are now deprecated. Functions named _, including the _ alias of gettext, are not affected.

sect3.title: Third argument to define()
sect3.simpara: Passing the case_insensitive argument to define is now deprecated. Case-insensitive constants were removed in PHP 8.0, since when the argument has been ignored. Explicitly passing &false; now emits a deprecation notice. Passing &true; continues to emit a warning, whose message now states that this will become an error in PHP 9.0. Omit the argument.

sect3.title: is_a() and is_subclass_of() with a string when allow_string is false
sect3.simpara: Calling is_a or is_subclass_of with a string as the first argument while allow_string is &false; is now deprecated. In that case the functions always return &false;, even when the class is already loaded, so such a call indicates a bug. To avoid triggering autoloading, check class_exists with autoloading disabled first, and then call the function with allow_string set to &true;.

sect3.title: metaphone()
sect3.simpara: The metaphone function is now deprecated. It implements the original 1990 Metaphone algorithm, which is limited to English pronunciation rules and has long been superseded by Double Metaphone and Metaphone 3. Phonetic algorithms are language-specific and frequently updated, so they are better served by a userland library; use one instead.

sect3.title: More than 16 filters in a php://filter URL
sect3.simpara: Using more than 16 filters in a php://filter URL without configuring the filter.max_filter_count stream context option now emits a deprecation notice. Long filter chains have no known legitimate use, but are the basis of a class of attacks that turn a local file inclusion or an arbitrary file read into remote code execution. When filter.max_filter_count is set explicitly, exceeding it is already an error: opening the stream fails with a warning.

Code that needs more filters should either add them with stream_filter_append or stream_filter_prepend, which are not limited, or raise the limit through the context option, for example globally with stream_context_set_default.

sect3.title: Passing objects to array_walk(), array_walk_recursive(), and http_build_query()
sect3.simpara: Passing an object as the array argument to array_walk or array_walk_recursive is now deprecated. A small number of functions silently interpret an object as the array of its visible properties. Modifying such properties through a by-reference callback violates readonly semantics and can corrupt enum cases, and array_walk_recursive does not recurse into nested objects anyway. Call get_object_vars on the object first and pass the resulting array.

Passing an object as the data argument to http_build_query is now deprecated. Objects encountered as values within data now also emit a deprecation notice when they are interpreted as arrays. Treating objects as arrays has been a recurring source of confusion, in particular for Stringable objects, which users expect to be converted to a string instead. Convert objects to arrays with get_object_vars, recursively if necessary, before calling the function.

sect3.title: is_double(), is_long(), is_integer(), and doubleval()
sect3.para:
Following the deprecation of the non-canonical cast names in PHP 8.5, the function aliases that carry the same outdated type names are now deprecated. They behave identically to their canonical counterparts, which should be used instead:
is_double => is_float is_long => is_int is_integer => is_int doubleval => floatval

sect3.title: strcoll() and SORT_LOCALE_STRING
sect3.simpara: The strcoll function is now deprecated. It compares strings according to the LC_COLLATE setting of the current locale, which is global process state set via setlocale that any library can change, it is not binary safe unlike every other string comparison function, and some locales do not implement correct collation rules. Use Collator::compare from the intl extension instead, which is accurate and has up-to-date collation rules.
sect3.para:
The SORT_LOCALE_STRING flag of the sort functions is now deprecated for the same reasons, as it sorts using strcoll. Use one of the following methods of the Collator class instead:
Collator::sort Collator::asort Collator::sortWithSortKeys

sect2.title: Bzip2
sect2.simpara: Passing an object as the parameters of the bzip2.compress and bzip2.decompress stream filters is now deprecated, as only an associative array is documented and supported. Call get_object_vars on the object first and pass the resulting array.

sect2.title: GMP
sect2.simpara: The shift (<<, >>) and exponentiation (**) operators on GMP objects now emit a deprecation notice when the right operand is a float whose conversion to int loses precision, consistent with the deprecation of implicit lossy float to int conversions elsewhere in the language.

sect2.title: MBString
sect2.para:
The mbregex functions have been deprecated, because the underlying Oniguruma library is no longer maintained; its maintenance ended in April 2025. The functions will be removed in PHP 9.0. For most use cases the PCRE functions with the u modifier are a suitable replacement. The affected functions are:
mb_ereg mb_ereg_match mb_ereg_replace mb_ereg_replace_callback mb_ereg_search mb_ereg_search_getpos mb_ereg_search_getregs mb_ereg_search_init mb_ereg_search_pos mb_ereg_search_regs mb_ereg_search_setpos mb_eregi mb_eregi_replace mb_regex_encoding mb_regex_set_options mb_split
sect2.simpara: The MB_ONIGURUMA_VERSION constant and the mbstring.regex_retry_limit and mbstring.regex_stack_limit INI directives are deprecated along with them.

Passing an object as the vars argument to mb_convert_variables is now deprecated, as objects are silently interpreted as the array of their visible properties. Call get_object_vars on the object first, or use mb_convert_encoding, which converts arrays recursively and returns the result instead of modifying its argument in place.

sect2.title: MySQLi
sect2.simpara: The mysqli_get_charset function and the mysqli::get_charset method are now deprecated, without replacement. They expose internal implementation details of the character set that have been meaningless since the switch to mysqlnd; in particular the reported collation does not correspond to the collation defined by the server. To get the name of the current character set, use mysqli_character_set_name or mysqli::character_set_name.

The mysqli_stmt_init function and the mysqli::stmt_init method are now deprecated. They create an empty statement object that still has to be prepared before use, and are a source of statement objects left in an inconsistent state. Use mysqli_prepare or mysqli::prepare instead, which prepare the statement in one step. For the same reason, calling the mysqli_stmt::__construct constructor without the query parameter is now deprecated; pass the query to the constructor instead.

sect2.title: Reflection
sect2.simpara: Calling ReflectionProperty::setValue or ReflectionProperty::setRawValue with an object that is not an instance of the class on which the property was declared is now deprecated. Unlike the other ReflectionProperty methods, which throw for such objects, these methods silently set a property on the unrelated object, which is no better than a normal assignment and conceptually wrong.

Passing an object to ReflectionMethod::invoke or ReflectionMethod::invokeArgs when invoking a static method is now deprecated. Static methods have no $this, so the object was ignored entirely and never validated. Pass &null; instead.

sect2.title: Session
sect2.simpara: Passing an object that does not implement both the SessionIdInterface::create_sid and SessionUpdateTimestampHandlerInterface::validateId methods to session_set_save_handler is now deprecated, regardless of which interfaces the object declares. These methods are required for a save handler to behave correctly under session.use_strict_mode, which is enabled by default as of PHP 8.6 and mitigates session fixation.

Accordingly, a deprecation notice is now emitted when a class implements SessionHandlerInterface without defining the SessionIdInterface::create_sid or SessionUpdateTimestampHandlerInterface::validateId methods. In PHP 9.0 these methods will be moved from SessionIdInterface and SessionUpdateTimestampHandlerInterface into SessionHandlerInterface, where they will be required. Implement both methods on custom save handlers now.

sect2.title: SPL
sect2.simpara: The spl_classes function is now deprecated. No other extension exposes such a function, and the Reflection extension is always available. Use ReflectionExtension::getClassNames instead.

The spl_object_hash function is now deprecated. Since PHP 8.1 its return value has been nothing more than a reformatted spl_object_id, and the name is misleading as the value is not derived from the contents of the object. The string form is also error-prone: two hashes can compare loosely equal because both are numeric strings. Use spl_object_id instead.
sect2.para:
The following ArrayIterator methods are now deprecated. They only exist because ArrayIterator historically shared its implementation with ArrayObject; most of them make little sense on an iterator and prevent optimizing its implementation. The corresponding ArrayObject methods are not deprecated.
ArrayIterator::getFlags ArrayIterator::setFlags ArrayIterator::asort ArrayIterator::ksort ArrayIterator::uasort ArrayIterator::uksort ArrayIterator::natsort ArrayIterator::natcasesort ArrayIterator::unserialize ArrayIterator::serialize

The CSV methods of SplFileObject are now deprecated. Their historical design inconsistencies, further exposed by named arguments, have made them increasingly difficult to maintain, and CSV handling does not naturally belong in SplFileObject. Use fgetcsv and fputcsv on a stream instead.
SplFileObject::fgetcsv SplFileObject::fputcsv SplFileObject::setCsvControl SplFileObject::getCsvControl

sect2.title: Zlib
sect2.simpara: Passing an object as the parameters of the zlib.deflate and zlib.inflate stream filters is now deprecated, as only an associative array is documented and supported. Call get_object_vars on the object first and pass the resulting array.

Passing an object as the options argument to deflate_init or inflate_init is now deprecated, as objects are silently interpreted as the array of their visible properties. Call get_object_vars on the object first and pass the resulting array.
